After 5 years of holding, PEA gains are exempt from income tax; only social levies of 18.6% remain due. What criteria should you use to choose a bank for your PEA? Here are the main points to weigh up in order to choose well: Brokerage and management fees This is criterion number one. High fees eat directly into your gains. Can you open a PEA without a linked current account? Opening a PEA without a linked current account is possible at some banks. This option can be attractive for those who want the benefits of a PEA without having to open a current account at the same bank. Options and restrictions Note that not all banks offer this. Some require a linked current account in order to open a PEA. Others, notably online banks, allow a PEA to be opened on its own. It is therefore essential to check before choosing. Be aware too that opening a PEA without a linked current account can come with certain restrictions. Transfer operations may be more limited, for instance, and management fees may be higher. It is therefore important to understand the specific terms of each offer before deciding. Comparing what banks offer on this What banks offer regarding a PEA without a linked current account can vary considerably. Some charge very competitive management fees, while others offer a wide range of investment options. It is therefore essential to compare offers to find the one that best matches your needs and investor profile. Fortuneo, for example, requires a minimum deposit of €1 at opening and charges brokerage fees from 0.35% of the amount (Starter tier). Boursorama (BoursoBank) requires a minimum deposit of €10 at opening and charges brokerage fees from €1.99 per order (Découverte tier). BforBank, which used to offer this option, no longer accepts new PEA applications since September 2023; only earlier holders keep their contract on its original terms. In conclusion, opening a PEA without a linked current account is an option that can suit some investors. It is essential, however, to understand the specific terms of each offer and to compare the options before deciding. For more on the best online banks, see our detailed comparison . How can you reduce the fees on your PEA? Always try to negotiate your contracts To reduce the fees on your PEA, negotiate with your bank, compare offers and choose a broker suited to how often you trade. Here are the concrete levers to pull. Ways to negotiate fees with your bank Point to your history as a customer : if you have banked there a long time, the bank may be willing to offer you better terms to keep your loyalty. Compare offers : show your bank that you know what competitors charge. That can serve as leverage in the negotiation. Consolidate your accounts : if you hold several accounts or savings products at the same bank, ask for a reduction in PEA fees as a priority customer. Negotiate when transferring : if you are considering transferring your PEA, that is the ideal moment to negotiate fees. Banks are often willing to offer better terms to attract new customers. Use scheduled investing : at Trade Republic, scheduled ETF orders carry no brokerage fees, ideal for investing a little each month without eating into your gains. Watch for promotional offers : reimbursed transfer fees or free orders come round regularly. Saxo Banque, for instance, offers zero fees on a selection of shares until 31 December 2026. Group your orders : rather than multiplying small transactions, place larger, less frequent orders to limit fixed fees. Hunt down hidden fees : read the fee schedule to spot custody fees, inactivity fees or withdrawal fees before opening. Before choosing, keep in mind the four habits that make the difference over the long run: Compare brokerage and management fees , which weigh directly on returns Assess the services : range of securities, platform quality, support responsiveness Check the soundness and reputation of the institution Start from your own profile : beginner or experienced, self-directed or managed, rare or frequent orders Within a PEA, the real enemy of your return is not the market, it is fees. A few euros per order and zero custody fees, repeated over twenty years, make the difference between a good and an excellent investment. Compare, transfer if you need to, and stay the course. Frequently asked questions Which bank is cheapest for a PEA in 2026? Bourse Direct is generally the cheapest broker, with brokerage fees from €0.99 per order and no custody fees. Fortuneo and BoursoBank follow closely, with no management fees. The actual ranking depends on the size and frequency of your orders. Can you open a PEA without a current account at the same bank? Yes, several online brokers allow a PEA to be opened on its own, without a linked current account. Others require one. Check this before opening, along with any resulting transfer constraints. Which fees should you watch on a PEA? Four items weigh on returns: brokerage fees per order, management or account-keeping fees, any custody fees, and transfer fees. Online brokers often reduce the last three to zero. How do you transfer a PEA from one bank to another? The transfer is requested from the receiving bank, which handles the process while preserving the plan's tax seniority. Allow several weeks and expect transfer fees at the departing bank, sometimes reimbursed by the new one. What is the taxation of a PEA after 5 years in 2026? After 5 years of holding, gains are exempt from income tax on withdrawal. Only social levies, raised to 18.6% on 1 January 2026 , remain due. Before 5 years, a withdrawal triggers heavier taxation. Self-directed or managed for your PEA? Self-directed management suits independent investors who pick their own securities, at lower cost. A managed-portfolio service, offered by Fortuneo or Yomoni, delegates the decisions to a manager in exchange for higher annual fees, around 0.6% to 1.6%. As more laws on sustainability, such as Taxonomy hit the market and stakeholders emphasise working only with responsible brands, your organisation has to make the right decision and effectively manage ESG impacts. However, some companies are not ready to or find implementing ESG a big challenge. Fortunately, ESG consulting for corporate clients is making a positive change by helping businesses to understand sustainability, its application, and reducing negative impacts. The ESG and sustainability consulting market is predicted to grow by 17% from 2022-2027. By 2027, the global market for ESG consultancy is expected to reach USD16 billion. Keep reading as we explain everything you need to know about ESG consulting for corporate clients. What is ESG Consulting? Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) cover the strategies and models that companies use to align their operations with the growing demand for sustainability. The interest by companies has risen over the years, ushering in a series of positive impacts not just for the respective companies but also for their partners, communities, and the entire planet. About 89% of business executives indicate that adopting ESG helps them win a competitive advantage in the market. Operating sustainably can also help your company to cut down the cost of production and get more support from investors. But even with these notable benefits, many companies struggle with ESG policy formulation and reporting. As a result, concerns have been raised about the rising problem of greenwashing . Environmental, social and governance (ESG) consulting for corporate clients comes as a reliable solution for guiding companies in planning and correctly implementing ESG strategies. The agencies are run by professionals who understand the process of ESG implementation and help companies to maximise the benefits that come from making their operations sustainable. Roles of ESG Consulting for Corporate Clients So, what can ESG consultants do for your company or corporate clients? Below are some of the main responsibilities and duties of ESG consultants and how they add value to your enterprise: Preparing ESG Policy For a company to operate sustainably, it needs to have a clear ESG policy . This is a clearly defined outline to guide a company’s sustainability efforts. An agency can help your company to review its operations and craft the best guidelines to ensure all the goals for sustainability are achieved. For example, the policy might set guidelines for zero-waste and zero-carbon emissions from all the units of the company or business. Performing ESG Risk Analysis ESG consultants can help advise you on the risk issues and how they should be addressed. In many cases, managers only focus on the positive impacts of ESG, such as cutting down emissions to address climate change, but this does not give the true outlook of the company to stakeholders. ESG consulting for corporate clients helps to change this by ensuring that all impacts, including the negative ones, are highlighted. ESG Reporting One of the crucial tasks of an ESG process is communication to stakeholders. Because ESG reporting is a process that involves a lot of planning, data gathering, and analysis, most companies find it pretty challenging. An ESG consultant can help you to understand the entire process of disclosure, from company assessment and materiality assessment to publishing of the ESG report . Next, they will work with your corporate team to craft a good strategy for ESG reporting and develop management insights for reducing sustainability risks. A good ESG consultancy can also come in handy in helping you to optimise the benefits of your ESG reports. For example, you can use the ESG report and ESG rating to drive the marketing of your company. This might be all you need to win a bigger market and profits. Today, some consultancies only work with specific industries to guarantee better results. For example, there are some firms that specialise in energy, hospitality, or financial industry, among other areas, with a focus on sustainability. Even with the agencies that focus on your niche, it is still critical to carry out due diligence and pick the best performer. Commitment to customer value. Before signing the contractual agreement, talk with the management of the agency to gauge its commitment to delivering value. title: Keith Clark Recognized for Decades of Advancing Aviation Fuel Safety
summary: Flight Safety Foundation recognizes Keith Clark’s decades of contribution to aviation fuel safety by awarding him the 2026 Business Aviation Meritorious Service Award.
body_text: Recognized for helping advance the future of aviation fuel safety, Keith Clark, senior quality control and technical representative at Phillips 66® Aviation, received the prestigious Business Aviation Meritorious Service Award at the 2026 Annual Flight Safety Foundation Business Safety Summit. This highly respected honor celebrates trailblazers who are elevating safety standards, driving meaningful change and helping propel business aviation forward through innovation, leadership and a relentless commitment to excellence. Clark now joins a distinguished group of aviation leaders, innovators and changemakers who continue influencing the future of flight safety. Clark’s decades-long commitment to aviation fuel safety has helped shape industry conversations around misfueling prevention, fueling best practices and safety education. From championing the ‘ Save a Life – Verify Fuel Type ’ public service misfueling prevention campaign to supporting online training resources through TrustedFuel.com , Clark has helped keep fuel safety top of mind for pilots, FBOs and aviation professionals nationwide while reinforcing a stronger culture of safety across business aviation. “Fuel safety has always been more than a job to me – it’s been a lifelong commitment,” said Keith Clark, Senior Quality Control and Technical Representative, Aviation, Phillips 66. “I’m deeply honored to receive this recognition from the Flight Safety Foundation and proud to be part of an industry that continues to prioritize safety and operational excellence.” With more than 40 years at Phillips 66® Aviation, Clark has dedicated his career to advancing fuel quality standards, strengthening safe fueling practices and helping raise the bar for aviation fuel safety across the industry. Throughout the years, he has collaborated with industry groups, pilots, FBOs and aviation leaders to expand safety education, share best practices and help drive meaningful progress throughout business aviation. “It’s exciting to see Keith Clark recognized for the incredible impact he has made on aviation fuel safety throughout his career,” said Jennifer Claunch, Manager, Aviation Sales, Phillips 66. “Keith’s passion, expertise and tireless commitment to safety have helped move the industry forward for decades. He’s not only helped set the standard for fuel safety, but has also inspired others across aviation to keep pushing it even higher.” Continuing that mission of education and industry engagement, Clark will next present “Bob Hoover: Perfecting Flight” at EAA AirVenture Oshkosh. Attendees can hear him speak on Thursday, July 23, from 8:30 to 9:45 a.m. at the EAA Museum Skyscape Theater. As Phillips 66® Aviation approaches its centennial milestone in 2027, Clark is looking toward the future by advancing fuel safety initiatives, strengthening quality assurance efforts and helping inspire the next generation of aviation professionals committed to keeping the industry flying safely forward.

title: When a Drone Is Recovered, the Clock Starts
summary: Field drone investigations turns a recovered UAV into an actionable lead in under four minutes -- no lab, no connectivity required. See how law enforcement agencies are closing cases faster.
body_text: Blog / When a Drone Is Recovered, the Clock Starts When a Drone Is Recovered, the Clock Starts July 27, 2026 | Brent Salo Email Key Takeaways: Drone recovery is the start, not the end – and the window to act on the data inside is measured in minutes, not hours. A recovered drone carries more intelligence than most agencies realize. Lab workflows weren’t built for drone forensics. Field-ready forensic tools extract GPS home points and full flight histories in under four minutes, with no lab, no connectivity and no specialist required. Detection without forensics only tells half the story. Drone forensics tells you who sent it, where it came from and what it did — and that’s what closes cases. In drone investigations, the most critical moments happen immediately after recovery. Drone forensics – the extraction and analysis of digital data from recovered UAVs – is what turns a hardware recovery into an actionable investigative lead. Law enforcement agencies have made real progress in countering drone threats. Detection systems are more capable, and interdiction efforts are improving. More drones are being identified, tracked and brought down across prisons, borders and critical infrastructure environments. Recovery of the device marks the beginning of the most time-sensitive phase of the investigation. When a drone is recovered, the clock starts. A Recovered Drone is a Live Lead At the moment of recovery, a drone is an active investigative lead. The device can be full of data officers can act on immediately: GPS coordinates that can place the operator within a meter of a launch site Full flight paths showing the where the drone originated and where it traveled Onboard video and photo files that may reveal targets, accomplices or contraband drops Device and account identifiers linked to mobile devices Data artifacts that may connect to a broader criminal network The problem is that most recovered drones never get this far. They’re tagged, bagged and shelved — processed as hardware exhibits the same as seized contraband. The data equivalent of a confession is then left unread and sitting in an evidence room. Why Drone Data Expires Fast Unlike a hard drive or a phone, a recovered drone comes with a clock running. The value of drone data is highest in the first few minutes of recovery. The malicious operator may still be nearby, the staging location may still be active and associated individuals may still be in motion. Traditional forensic workflows are built for depth, not speed: send the device to a lab, wait 48 to 72 hours, receive a report. For most investigation types, that’s exactly right. But in drone forensics, it often means the window has already closed by the time the analysis comes back. It’s not a critique of lab workflows, it’s just a different kind of problem. Drone intelligence is time-sensitive in a way that most digital evidence isn’t. The question is whether your team has a tool that can match that pace. What Field Drone Forensics Looks Like in Practice The shift to field-ready forensics has moved the analysis from the lab to the scene, and that changes what’s possible in the first hour of an investigation. A purpose-built field forensics tool extracts and decodes UAV data at the point of collection: no lab, no connectivity, no specialist required. The officer who recovers the drone can start pulling intelligence before they’ve finished processing the scene. In practice, that means: Extracting flight logs within minutes, including launch coordinates, route and landing zone Identifying the GPS home point and moving directly toward a potential operator location Reviewing onboard video and photo files while the incident area is still active Capturing controller and device identifiers to support immediate follow-on mobile investigation Visualizing flight paths to guide search and response decisions in real time This is even better when the same device can handle mobile devices, SIM cards and portable media, so you don’t have to juggle separate kits if the drone and a suspect’s phone are both in custody. It has directly resulted in multiple convictions in the UK, relating to a broad range of offences, including prison incursions, criminal damage and UAV flight offences. Daniel Hurley, Digital Forensic Examiner, Eastern Region Special Operations Unit (ERSOU) The Legal Framework for Drone Enforcement Is Expanding If your agency is being cautious about drone forensics because the legal framework felt uncertain, that picture is shifting. Regulatory authority for drone enforcement is expanding across multiple jurisdictions — in the U.S. through the SAFER SKIES Act, and internationally through updated enforcement guidance from bodies including Europol and EASA. The practical result is clear: More drones will be lawfully intercepted More digital evidence will be recovered More investigations will depend on how quickly that evidence is acted upon Agencies that already have field-ready forensic capability are positioned to take full advantage of that expanded authority. Does Drone Evidence Hold Up in Court? Even under time pressure, evidence must meet the standards that come after the scene. Drone evidence faces the same admissibility requirements as any digital evidence: there must be documented chain of custody, validated extraction methodology and forensically sound output in formats already accepted in court and evidentiary proceedings across jurisdictions worldwide. Cut corners in the field, and you can run the risk of the case falling apart downstream. The right field forensics tool doesn’t force a tradeoff between speed and integrity. It delivers both. T he Bottom Line When a drone is recovered, the most important question is what can be done next, and how quickly. Drone investigations aren’t a new category of work, they are mobile forensics investigations with a shorter clock. The evidence is rich, the intelligence is actionable and the window to use it is narrow. Agencies that are already doing strong mobile forensics work have most of the foundation in place. The missing piece is usually the right tool at the right point in the process. Every Drone Has a Story. Make Sure You Can Tell It. Frequently Asked Questions About Drone Forensics What is drone forensics? Drone forensics is the extraction and analysis of digital data from recovered unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). That data includes GPS flight logs, operator coordinates, onboard video and photo media, device and account identifiers and telemetry records. Drone forensics turns a hardware seizure into a prosecution-ready evidence package by connecting the recovered drone to the operator, the launch site and the network behind it. What data can be extracted from a seized drone? A recovered UAV can contain GPS home points and full flight histories, altitude and speed telemetry, onboard video and photo files, cell tower connection records, controller and app identifiers and account data from the operator’s connected mobile device. The exact data available depends on the drone model, firmware version and how the device was configured at the time of the incident. How quickly can drone data be extracted in the field? With a purpose-built field forensics tool, GPS home point and full flight history extraction from a seized drone can be completed within minutes. That speed is the core operational advantage of field-based drone forensics over lab-based workflows, which typically require 48 to 72 hours or more — by which point the operator and the staging location may be long gone. Is drone forensics evidence admissible in court? Yes, when collected properly. Drone forensic evidence must meet the same standards as any digital evidence: documented chain of custody, validated extraction methodology and forensically sound output. Purpose-built forensic tools produce industry-standard output in the same globally accepted formats trusted by law enforcement and legal systems around the world. If requested, CFID produced DD and E01 forensic outputs. The method and tool used for collection matters — improvised or non-forensic extraction may be challenged at trial. What is the SAFER SKIES Act and what does it mean for law enforcement? The SAFER SKIES Act, signed into law in December 2025 as part of the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act, grants state and local law enforcement agencies legal authority to detect, track and mitigate drone threats for the first time. The Act establishes a defined legal framework for counter-drone operations at the state and local level, expanding the evidentiary opportunity for agencies that have the forensic capability to act on the drones they bring down. Federal funding is available to help agencies build that capability. Learn more here . What is the difference between counter-drone technology and drone forensics? Counter-drone technology — detection systems, tracking radar and disabling equipment — tells you a drone is present and can in some cases bring it down. Drone forensics is what happens after: the extraction and analysis of the digital data on the recovered device. Counter-drone capability without forensic capability means agencies can stop a threat but cannot identify who sent it, build a prosecution-ready case or disrupt the broader network behind it. title: What is Automatic Speech Recognition? A Comprehensive Overview of ASR Technology
summary: This article aims to answer the question: What is ASR?, and provide a comprehensive overview of Automatic Speech Recognition technology.
body_text: Automatic Speech Recognition, also known as ASR, is the use of AI technology to process human speech into readable text. The field has grown exponentially over the past decade, and market projections show it's expected to reach a market volume of US$73 billion by 2031. ASR systems now power applications we use every day—from TikTok and Instagram's real-time captions to Spotify's podcast transcriptions and Zoom's meeting notes. As ASR approaches human accuracy levels, we're seeing an explosion of applications taking advantage of this technology to make audio and video data more accessible. Speech-to-text APIs like AssemblyAI are making ASR technology more affordable, accessible, and accurate for developers and businesses of all sizes. This comprehensive guide covers the fundamentals of Automatic Speech Recognition technology. You'll learn what ASR is and how it evolved, understand the technical approaches that power modern systems, and discover how businesses are using this technology today. We'll also explore current challenges and what's coming next in the field of speech recognition. What is Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR)? A Brief History Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) is AI technology that converts spoken language into written text by analyzing audio waveforms and identifying patterns in human speech. Modern ASR systems can transcribe conversations in real-time with accuracy approaching human-level performance. Early research confirms ASR extends back to 1952 when Bell Labs created "Audrey," a digit recognizer that could identify spoken numbers, though it required users to pause after each digit. Audrey could only transcribe spoken numbers, but a decade later, researchers improved upon the system so it could transcribe rudimentary spoken words like "hello." For most of the past fifteen years, ASR was powered by classical machine learning technologies like Hidden Markov Models. Though once the industry standard, accuracy of these classical models had plateaued in recent years. This plateau opened the door for advanced AI technology that's also powered breakthroughs in self-driving cars. In 2014, Baidu published the landmark paper, Deep Speech: Scaling up end-to-end speech recognition . The paper's published results , which achieved a 16% error rate on a standard benchmark, demonstrated AI's power in speech recognition and kicked off a renaissance in ASR. This AI-powered approach pushed model accuracy past the plateau and closer to human-level performance. Not only has accuracy skyrocketed, but access to ASR technology has also improved dramatically. Ten years ago, customers would have to engage in lengthy, expensive enterprise speech recognition software contracts to license ASR technology. Today, developers, startup companies, and Fortune 500s have access to advanced ASR technology via simple APIs like AssemblyAI's speech-to-text API . Test Speech-to-Text in Your Browser Upload audio or video and see accurate transcripts in seconds—no code required. Explore ASR capabilities hands-on before integrating the API. Try it here Let's look more closely at the two dominant approaches to ASR and understand how they work. How ASR Works Today, there are two main approaches to Automatic Speech Recognition: Traditional Hybrid Approach : Uses separate lexicon, acoustic, and language models working together ‍ End-to-End AI Approach: Employs a single unified model that directly maps audio to text Understanding these differences helps explain why modern ASR systems achieve such impressive accuracy. Traditional Hybrid Approach The traditional hybrid approach is the legacy approach to speech recognition and dominated the field for the past fifteen years. Many companies still rely on this approach simply because it's the way it has always been done—there's extensive research and training data available, despite plateaus in accuracy. Here's how the traditional approach works: Traditional HMM and GMM Systems Traditional HMM (Hidden Markov Models) and GMM (Gaussian Mixture Models) require forced aligned data. Force alignment determines where in time particular words occur in an audio segment. This approach combines three separate models: Lexicon Model: Describes phonetic pronunciation of words Acoustic Model: Predicts phonemes from audio segments Language Model: Predicts word sequences and probabilities Lexicon Model The lexicon model describes how words are pronounced phonetically. You need a custom phoneme set for each language, handcrafted by expert phoneticians. Acoustic Model The acoustic model (AM) models the acoustic patterns of speech. The job of the acoustic model is to predict which sound or phoneme is being spoken at each speech segment from the forced aligned data. The acoustic model is usually of an HMM or GMM variant. Language Model The language model (LM) models the statistics of language. It learns which sequences of words are most likely to be spoken, and its job is to predict which words will follow on from the current words and with what probability. Decoding Decoding is a process of utilizing the lexicon, acoustic, and language models to produce a transcript. Downsides of the Traditional Approach Though still widely used, the traditional hybrid approach to speech recognition has several drawbacks. Lower accuracy is the biggest challenge. Each model must be trained independently, making them time and labor intensive. Forced aligned data is difficult to come by and requires significant human labor. Experts are needed to build custom phonetic sets to boost the model's accuracy. End-to-End AI Approach An end-to-end AI approach represents a newer way of thinking about ASR, and how we approach ASR here at AssemblyAI. How End-to-End AI Models Work With an end-to-end system, you can directly map a sequence of input acoustic features into a sequence of words. The data doesn't need to be force-aligned. Depending on the architecture, an AI system can be trained to produce accurate transcripts without a lexicon model and language model, although language models can help produce more accurate results. Modern Architectures: CTC, LAS, and RNNTs CTC, LAS, and RNNTs are popular speech recognition end-to-end AI architectures. These systems can be trained to produce highly accurate results without needing force aligned data, lexicon models, and language models. Advantages of End-to-End AI Models End-to-end AI models are easier to train and require less human labor than a traditional approach. They're also more accurate than the traditional models being used today. The AI research community is actively searching for ways to constantly improve these models using the latest research. There's no concern of accuracy plateaus any time soon—in fact, we'll see AI models reach human level accuracy in the next few years. Build with Accurate ASR APIs Leverage end-to-end AI models for reliable transcription across diverse audio. Create a free account and start transcribing in minutes. Start free Comparing Traditional vs. Modern ASR Approaches Aspect Traditional Hybrid End-to-End AI Components Lexicon + Acoustic + Language Models Single unified model Training Data Requires force-aligned data Works with unaligned audio-text pairs Human Labor High (phoneticians, alignment) Minimal Accuracy Trend Plateaued Continuously improving Setup Complexity High (multiple models) Lower (single system) Customization Requires expert knowledge Can be fine-tuned with data ASR Accuracy and Performance Metrics Not all ASR systems are created equal. The quality of transcription can make or break user experience. Word Error Rate (WER) is the industry standard for measuring ASR accuracy. It compares machine-generated transcripts to human-verified transcripts and calculates error percentage. The formula is simple: WER = (Substitutions + Deletions + Insertions) / Number of Words in Reference Transcript A lower WER means higher accuracy. For example, a WER of 10% means that 90% of the words were transcribed correctly. However, WER doesn't tell the whole story. Real-world audio presents multiple challenges: Background noise and poor audio quality Overlapping speakers and interruptions Unique accents and speaking styles Industry-specific jargon and terminology This is why one ASR system might feel seamless while another feels clumsy. Modern AI models, like AssemblyAI's Universal models, are trained on millions of hours of diverse audio data to perform reliably across these challenging conditions. ASR Key Terms and Features Acoustic Model: The acoustic model takes in audio waveforms and predicts what words are present in the waveform. Language Model : The language model can be used to help guide and correct the acoustic model's predictions. Word Error Rate : The industry standard measurement of how accurate an ASR transcription is, as compared to a human transcription. Speaker Diarization : Answers the question, who spoke when? Also referred to as speaker labels. Custom Vocabulary : Custom vocabulary boosts accuracy for a list of specific keywords or phrases when transcribing an audio file. Sentiment Analysis : The sentiment, typically positive, negative, or neutral, of specific speech segments in an audio or video file. See more models specific to AssemblyAI . Key Applications of ASR Modern ASR delivers measurable value across diverse industries. Key applications include: Telephony: Call tracking , cloud phone solutions, and contact centers need accurate transcriptions, as well as innovative analytical features like Conversation Intelligence , call analytics, speaker diarization, and more. Video Platforms: Real-time and asynchronous video captioning are industry standard. Video editing platforms (and video editors alike) also need content categorization and content moderation to improve accessibility and search. Media Monitoring : Speech-to-text APIs can help broadcast TV, podcasts, radio, and more quickly and accurately detect brand and other topic mentions for better advertising. Virtual Meetings : Meeting platforms like Zoom, Google Meet, WebEx, and more need accurate transcriptions and the ability to analyze this content to drive key insights and action. Choosing a Speech-to-Text API With more APIs on the market, how do you know which speech-to-text API is best for your application ? When considering which API to use, one insights report found that the top factors for buyers are cost, quality, accuracy, and ease of use. Key considerations to keep in mind include: How accurate the API is What additional models are offered What kind of support you can expect Pricing and documentation transparency Data security Company innovation Companies like Aloware use highly accurate ASR to power smart transcription and speed up QA for their customers. CallRail doubled its Conversational Intelligence customers by integrating AI-powered ASR into its platform and building powerful Generative AI products on top of the transcription data. Marvin added AI transcription to build a suite of AI-powered tools and features that resulted in significantly less time analyzing research data for its customers. Challenges of ASR Today One of the main challenges of ASR today is the continual push toward human accuracy levels. While both ASR approaches—traditional hybrid and end-to-end AI—are significantly more accurate than ever before, neither can claim 100% human accuracy. There's so much nuance in the way we speak, from dialects to slang to pitch. Even the best AI models can't be trained to cover this long tail of edge cases without significant effort. Some think they can solve this accuracy problem with custom speech-to-text models . However, unless you have a very specific use case, like children's speech, custom models are actually less accurate, harder to train, and more expensive in practice than a good end-to-end AI model. Another top concern is speech-to-text privacy for APIs . In fact, a recent industry survey found that over 30% of respondents cited data privacy as a significant challenge, as many large ASR companies use customer data to train models without explicit permission. Continual data storage in the cloud also raises concerns over potential security breaches, especially if raw audio or video files or transcription text contains Personally Identifiable Information. On the Horizon for ASR As the field of ASR continues to grow, we can expect to see greater integration of speech-to-text technology into our everyday lives, as well as more widespread industry applications. We're already seeing advancements in ASR and related AI fields taking place at an accelerated rate. Examples include OpenAI's ChatGPT, HuggingFace spaces and AI applications , and AssemblyAI's Universal model . In regards to model building, we also expect to see a shift to a self-supervised learning system to solve some of the challenges with accuracy discussed above. End-to-end AI models are data hungry. Our Universal model at AssemblyAI, for example, is trained on millions of hours of raw audio and video training data for industry-best accuracy levels. However, obtaining human transcriptions for this same training data would be almost impossible given the time constraints associated with human processing speeds. This is where self-supervised AI systems can help. Essentially, this is a way to get an abundance of unlabeled data and build a foundational model on top of it. Then, since we have statistical knowledge of the data, we can fine-tune it on downstream tasks with a smaller amount of data, making it a more accessible approach to model building. This is an exciting possibility with profound implications for the field. If this transition occurs, expect ASR models to become even more accurate and affordable, making their use and acceptance more widespread. Ready to experience the power of modern ASR technology? Try our API for free and see how accurate speech recognition can transform your applications. Frequently Asked Questions About Automatic Speech Recognition What is the difference between ASR and NLP? ASR converts spoken audio into written text, while NLP analyzes that text to understand meaning, intent, and sentiment. Think of ASR as the ears and NLP as the brain—they work together in Voice AI applications. Is ASR the same as speech-to-text? Yes, ASR and speech-to-text are used interchangeably. ASR is the underlying technology, while speech-to-text describes the function it performs. What is the difference between speech recognition and voice recognition? Speech recognition transcribes what is being said, while voice recognition identifies who is speaking by matching unique voiceprints. Speech recognition creates transcripts; voice recognition labels speakers. Is ASR a form of AI? Yes, modern ASR uses AI models to convert human speech into text. The most advanced ASR systems use sophisticated AI architectures that continuously learn and improve from vast amounts of audio data. How accurate is modern ASR compared to humans? Modern ASR systems achieve Word Error Rates below 5% on clear audio, approaching human-level accuracy in ideal conditions. Performance varies with background noise, accents, and overlapping speakers, where humans still maintain advantages in contextual understanding. ‍

title: Days Sales Outstanding Benchmarks for Dental Practices in 2026
body_text: Days sales outstanding benchmarks for dental practices: under 25 days is excellent, 25–30 days is good, 30–45 days is the industry average, and over 45 days signals a revenue cycle breakdown requiring immediate action. Solo practices typically run 40–60 days DSO; top-performing DSO organizations with centralized billing consistently hit under 25 days. Group practices with standardized billing workflows typically land at 30–45 days. This guide covers the complete DSO benchmarks by practice type, the AR aging targets that underpin them, and seven proven strategies to reduce your dental days in AR to top-quartile performance. Production is up, the schedule is full, but cash is tight that's the signature of a high-DSO practice. DSO measures how long it takes to collect payment after delivering a service, and most practices carry far more locked-up revenue in unpaid claims and patient balances than they realize. Most dental practices average 30–45 days DSO industry best practice is under 30 days, and top-performing DSO organizations consistently hit under 25. Insurance denial rates climbed from 11% (2022) to 15% (2026) , meaning practices are fighting harder to collect revenue they've already earned. The fastest DSO gains come upstream: 48-hour insurance pre-verification, same-day claim submission, and capturing every inbound call before a scheduling error becomes a billing failure. Key Takeaways Benchmark the right range: Most dental practices average 30–45 days DSO industry best practice is under 30 days, and top-performing DSO organizations consistently hit under 25 days. Aging AR is largely unrecoverable: Only 15–25% of balances past 90 days are typically collected, making early intervention critical to your cash flow. Denial rates are rising: Insurance denial rates in dentistry climbed from roughly 11% in 2022 to approximately 15% in 2024–2026, directly inflating dental days in AR across the industry. Patient balances are under-collected: The industry average patient collection rate runs 70–80% the target is 90%+, leaving thousands in uncollected revenue per month. Practice type matters: Solo practices typically run 40–60 days DSO; group practices 30–45 days; top-performing DSO organizations hit under 25 days with centralized billing. 85%+ of your AR belongs in the 0–30 day bucket: Anything less signals a revenue cycle breakdown that will compound over time. Upstream actions protect DSO: Capturing insurance data before the appointment and answering every inbound call are two of the highest-leverage actions for keeping the billing cycle clean from day one. AI receptionists sound human and collect billing data: Modern AI receptionists for dental practices handle scheduling calls naturally patients rarely know they're speaking with AI and collect insurance carrier, member ID, and date of birth during the call so billing starts with clean, verified data. What Is Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) in Dentistry? Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) measures the average number of days between delivering a dental service and receiving payment capturing how efficiently your revenue cycle converts production into cash. In dental billing, "days in AR" and "DSO" are often used interchangeably. The subtle distinction: DSO calculates collection velocity on credit sales, while AR days describes the overall aging of your outstanding balances. In practice, both metrics tell the same story about whether your billing cycle is working. DSO applies differently across practice structures: Solo practices tracks whether a small team is keeping up with claims and patient follow-up Dental groups reveals consistency (or inconsistency) across multiple locations DSO organizations benchmarks centralized billing office performance across the entire portfolio A DSO under 30 days means payments arrive quickly and your revenue cycle is healthy. A DSO over 45 days means earned revenue is sitting idle in unpaid claims and overdue patient balances that should and can be in your bank account. For context on how DSO intersects with patient experience, see dental DSO benchmarks and patient experience data. How We Built These 2026 DSO Benchmarks These benchmarks draw from our analysis of dental revenue cycle data across solo practices, multi-location groups, and DSO organizations. We cross-referenced findings against published industry reports: the Zentist 2026 RCM Trends Report, Dental Economics payment goal benchmarks, and Outsource Strategies International AR reporting. Our evaluation methodology: We scored practice performance across five criteria DSO days, AR aging distribution, collection rate, denial rate, and patient balance recovery. Each score was then mapped to a practice-type profile: solo, group, or DSO. Practices in the top quartile across all five criteria achieve under 25 days DSO consistently. The benchmarks here reflect what the best-run practices actually achieve. Each tier is a realistic, attainable target for a practice willing to invest in its revenue cycle. Practices that implement the strategies in this guide should expect measurable DSO improvement within 60–90 days. Full normalization of the AR aging report typically takes 4–6 months. How to Calculate Your Practice's DSO The dental practice DSO average is calculated with a simple formula, and running it monthly gives you more revenue cycle insight than almost any other metric. The formula: DSO = (Accounts Receivable ÷ Total Credit Sales) × Number of Days Worked example: If your practice has $75,000 in outstanding AR and $90,000 in total production last month: DSO = ($75,000 ÷ $90,000) × 30 = 25 days Excellent If the same practice had $150,000 in AR, the DSO would be 50 days a clear signal of billing delays or patient balances accumulating. Two calculation methods: Rolling 30-day method: Use the prior 30 days of collections as the denominator. Best for spotting month-to-month trends quickly. Countback method: Start from the most recent month and subtract monthly gross sales from the AR balance until it reaches zero, counting the applicable days. More accurate for longer-term benchmarking. Most practice management software including OpenDental, EagleSoft, Denticon, and CareStack can generate the AR and production figures you need automatically. Run this calculation monthly and compare it against the benchmark scorecard below. DSO Benchmarks for Dental Practices: 2026 Scorecard Use this table to locate your practice in the benchmark spectrum. Each tier reflects both DSO range and the collection rate that typically accompanies it. Revenue Cycle Performance Benchmarks Performance Tier DSO Range What It Means Collection Rate Excellent Under 25 days Top-tier performance; typical of centralized DSO billing offices with full RCM automation 98%+ Good 25–30 days High-performing group practice with standardized billing workflows 96–98% Acceptable 30–45 days Industry average; manageable but improvable; most practices land here 91–95% Poor 45–60 days Cash flow pressure; often indicates inconsistent follow-up or elevated denial rates 84–91% Critical 60+ days Significant RCM breakdown requiring immediate action; claims are aging and patient balances are escaping Below 84% Sources: Dental Economics benchmarking data ; Outsource Strategies International RCM reporting ; Dental Billing Assist KPI benchmarks What the tiers mean for your cash flow: Acceptable to Good is a realistic near-term target for most practices. The leap from 40 days to 28 days represents significant freed-up cash for a $90,000/month practice, that's roughly $36,000 no longer sitting in unpaid AR. Good to Excellent requires billing automation, consistent denial management, and clean claims submitted on the day of service. It's achievable but requires investment in process and tooling. Critical practices must treat DSO recovery as a practice-survival issue, not an optimization exercise. Immediate AR work-down of the 90+ day bucket is the first step. DSO Benchmarks by Practice Type: Solo, Group, and DSO Dental practice DSO averages differ meaningfully by practice structure because the available resources, staffing, and systems differ too. Solo Practices Typical DSO: 40–60 days Main challenges: One or two staff members managing scheduling, billing, and patient communication simultaneously. Manual claim submission, limited bandwidth for denial follow-up, and no dedicated billing role. Achievable target: 30–40 days with improved upfront insurance verification, same-day claim submission, and automated patient billing statements. The opportunity: Even a 10-day DSO improvement for a $90K/month solo practice frees $30,000 from AR real cash flow without adding staff. Group Practices (Multi-Location) Typical DSO: 30–45 days Main challenges: Inconsistent front-desk workflows across locations create variable billing quality. AR aging can look dramatically different at location A versus location B, making the aggregate DSO misleading. Achievable target: 25–35 days with centralized billing oversight, standardized workflows, and location-level AR reporting. See more on DSO call center strategy for multi-location dental groups. DSO Organizations Typical DSO: Under 25 days (top performers); 35–60 days (average, across all portfolio locations) Advantages: Centralized billing offices (CBOs), standardized denial management workflows, and RCM automation at scale give DSOs structural advantages that solo and group practices can't replicate with headcount alone. Achievable target: Under 25 days organization-wide with a functioning CBO, electronic remittance advice (ERA) posting, and consistent denial management. The gap between top-performing DSOs and average practices is primarily a workflow discipline gap, not a technology gap. Top performers run clean claims, follow up on every aging bucket, and catch denials before they pass 30 days regardless of their specific software stack. The most important DSO insight for practice operators: A well-run billing process in a centralized DSO billing office is the single most powerful driver of DSO reduction, capable of taking a portfolio from 45+ days to under 25 days without increasing headcount. AR Aging Benchmarks Beyond DSO DSO is your headline metric, but the AR aging report is the diagnostic that tells you where the breakdown is occurring. A healthy aging report for dental practices looks like this: AR Aging Bucket Targets Aging Bucket Target % of Total AR Risk if Exceeded 0–30 days 85%+ Low 31–60 days Under 10% Medium — active insurance follow-up required 61–90 days Under 5% High — patient balance escalation protocol needed 90+ days Under 3% Critical — only 15–25% of this bucket is recoverable Sources: Dental Economics payment goal benchmarks ; Pearly dental AR benchmarking The 90+ day rule is non-negotiable: Industry data consistently shows that only 15–25% of dental AR past 90 days is ever collected. Once a balance passes 120 days without resolution, recovery rates fall even further. The 90+ day bucket is the most unrecoverable segment in dental revenue cycle management the cost of ignoring it is not delayed cash, it is permanent write-off. AR ratio as a second check: Your total AR should not exceed one month's average production . A practice producing $90,000/month should carry no more than $90,000 in total AR (a 1.0x ratio). A ratio above 1.5x signals that production is outpacing collections a structural problem, not a temporary billing backlog. Key action thresholds: Any insurance claim past 30 days without a payer response → follow up immediately Any patient balance past 60 days without a payment arrangement → escalate to collections protocol Any aging bucket above target → identify the contributing payer or patient segment and address it specifically, not the AR report as a whole Clean Claims: Documentation, Compliance, and Verification High DSO is almost always downstream of upstream documentation failures. The industry standard for a clean claim requires specific documentation attached at submission and skipping any element adds days to your DSO. Clean Claim Documentation Requirements Every dental claim that is submitted without errors requires: Accurate CDT codes procedure codes must match the documented treatment and the payer's allowed code list Supporting clinical documentation X-rays, narrative descriptions, and periodontal charting for procedures that require them (extractions, implants, crowns, periodontal therapy) Pre-authorization confirmation many plans require pre-authorization for high-value procedures; submitting without it guarantees a denial Correct patient demographics date of birth, subscriber ID, and payer ID must match exactly what the payer has on file Provider credentials NPI, tax ID, and group/individual billing configuration must be correct and current A single missing field can trigger an automatic denial. The most effective prevention is real-time claim scrubbing before submission automated checking that catches missing or mismatched fields before the claim leaves the practice. Real-Time Eligibility Verification Real-time insurance eligibility verification is the highest-impact upstream intervention for reducing DSO. It confirms coverage, deductibles, frequency limitations, and benefit maximums electronically at the time of scheduling or check-in. Practices that verify eligibility before every appointment reduce eligibility-related denials by up to 60%. Best practice: verify 48–72 hours before the appointment. This allows time to correct errors before the patient arrives. Re-verify at check-in for same-day appointments. Modern systems OpenDental, Denticon, and CareStack support real-time eligibility checks through clearinghouse integrations. Compliance Considerations Dental billing systems handle protected health information (PHI) and financial data, requiring HIPAA compliance at every layer: EFT enrollment: Electronic funds transfer with major payers reduces payment turnaround by 5–10 days and eliminates virtual credit card fees that erode collections Secure patient billing: Automated billing platforms must use HIPAA-compliant encryption for patient statements and payment portals Role-based access controls: Billing staff should have access limited to the data required for their role a HIPAA requirement and an internal control that prevents errors and unauthorized changes DSO Limitations: What the Metric Doesn't Capture DSO is the best single-number summary of revenue cycle performance. But it has real limitations operators need to understand: It averages out location-level variance: A DSO of 35 days at the portfolio level can mask locations running at 18 days and others at 90 days. Location-level DSO tracking is essential for multi-site groups. It doesn't separate insurance from patient AR: High insurance AR and high patient AR require different interventions. Track them separately. It can look artificially good after write-offs: Writing off uncollectable balances improves DSO without actually improving collections. Track write-off rate alongside DSO to get the true picture. It doesn't capture production efficiency: A practice can improve DSO by reducing production more patients with faster cash cycles. Always benchmark DSO alongside collection rate and total production. What's Driving High DSO in 2026? Rising insurance denial rates, incomplete automation adoption, and front-desk staffing pressure are the three structural forces pushing dental practice DSO higher in 2026. Dental practices that managed a DSO of 35 days in 2022 may find themselves at 45–50 days in 2026 running the same processes. Three structural shifts explain why: Rising insurance denial rates. Claim denial rates in dentistry climbed from roughly 11% in 2022 to approximately 15% in 2024–2026, according to dental billing industry data . More than three-quarters of dental practices report experiencing increased claim denials or heightened payer scrutiny over the past 12 months, per the Zentist 2026 RCM Trends Report . Each denial adds days to the AR cycle and rising denial rates are the single most important external driver of DSO growth in 2026. Avoidable errors at the root. Industry reporting consistently shows that most dental claim denials are preventable typically the result of missing patient data, incorrect insurance information, or submission errors that could have been caught before the claim was ever sent. This is a billing process problem, not a payer problem. Implementing a pre-submission claim scrubbing step is the most direct way to eliminate this category of DSO inflation. Patient balance collection gaps. The average dental practice collects 70–80% of the patient-owed portion of a bill well below the 90%+ target. As insurance plans shift more cost responsibility to patients through higher deductibles and co-pays, this gap is widening. Automation adoption is still incomplete. Around 58% of dental practices committed to some form of RCM automation in 2026, per the Zentist RCM Trends Report via Dentistry Today. The remaining 42% are running manual processes that cannot keep pace with rising claim complexity and denial volume. Staffing pressure on the front desk. Front-desk turnover leaves billing tasks deprioritized and incoming patient information collected inconsistently. A missed call during a busy morning is also a billing setup failure an appointment that never got booked produces nothing for the revenue cycle to collect. How to Reduce DSO: 7 Proven Strategies These seven actions address the most common DSO drivers in dental practices. Implement them in order of leverage upstream actions first, downstream cleanup second. Verify insurance eligibility before every appointment. Confirming coverage, deductibles, co-pays, and benefit maximums 48–72 hours before the visit prevents the most common source of clean claim failures. Learn how to automate insurance verification for every scheduled patient without adding manual steps for your team. Submit clean claims on the day of service. Same-day claim submission is one of the highest-leverage billing habits available. Every day a claim sits unsubmitted is a day added to DSO. Use your PMS (OpenDental, EagleSoft, Denticon, or CareStack) to set automated end-of-day claim exports. Follow up on every claim past 30 days. No insurance claim should sit without a payer response for more than 30 days. Set a 30-day aging trigger in your billing workflow and assign specific ownership for follow-up. Automating billing inquiry management reduces the manual burden without requiring additional staff. Build a denial management workflow. Every denial should be categorized by reason code, corrected, and resubmitted within five business days. Track denial reasons by payer patterns reveal systemic issues with how a specific carrier is being billed, not just individual errors. Send patient statements within 7 days of insurance posting. Delayed patient billing is a leading cause of patient AR aging. Automated statement delivery via email, text, or paper shortens the patient billing cycle and dramatically reduces follow-up call volume. Collect at the point of service. Practices that collect the patient-owed portion at checkout eliminate a significant slice of patient AR before it can age. For larger balances, offer payment plans with automatic recurring payments not monthly manual collection attempts. Review the AR aging report weekly, not monthly. Monthly reviews are too slow: a claim can move from 30 to 60 days in a single billing cycle. Weekly reviews catch exceptions before they become write-offs. Assign a specific team member to own the aging report and act on exceptions within 48 hours. How Front-Desk Operations Affect Your DSO Most dental practices treat DSO as a billing department problem. The biggest leverage points, however, are upstream in how calls are answered, how appointments are booked, and how patient information is collected before billing begins. Missed calls inflate DSO mathematically. Dental practices miss up to 35% of inbound calls, according to call handling industry data . Each missed call can be a missed appointment and an appointment that never gets booked produces nothing. When total production decreases, DSO increases even if billing is running perfectly, because the denominator in the DSO formula (total credit sales) shrinks. Recapturing missed production directly improves your DSO calculation. Collecting insurance data on the scheduling call eliminates downstream errors. When patients call to book, capturing their insurance carrier, member ID, and date of birth at that moment lets your team verify eligibility 48 hours before the appointment rather than scrambling at check-in or discovering errors after the claim is submitted. Eligibility failures at check-in are a leading source of claim denials. Front-desk accuracy determines billing accuracy. If patient information is entered incorrectly during scheduling a wrong date of birth, a transposed subscriber ID that error flows into the claim. A denial 30 days later adds another 2–4 weeks to your DSO. Getting it right on the first call is the most cost-effective denial prevention available. Learn how to recover aged AR across insurance and patient balances to free up billing bandwidth during the recovery period. Frequently Asked Questions What is a good DSO for a dental practice? title: Your Quick Guide to the 2021 Open Enrollment Period
body_text: Categories Health Insurance / Healthcare / Medicare / Obamacare FAQ Your Quick Guide to the 2021 Open Enrollment Period By HealthSherpa Share this post Once a year, all eligible Americans get a chance to shop the Health Insurance Marketplace and get a Marketplace plan, also known as Obamacare or an Affordable Care Act plan. This time is known as the annual Open Enrollment Period (OEP). The Affordable Care Act (ACA) ensures that all eligible Americans get this opportunity once a year to buy affordable health coverage for themselves and their families. And the ACA also means that all plans available on the Marketplace offer the following key consumer protections: For 2021, the Open Enrollment Period runs from Sunday, November 1 through Tuesday, December 15, 2020 in most states. Coverage purchased during the OEP window will begin on January 1, 2021 You can shop available plans and compare prices here or enter your zip code below to see available plans. Who is eligible to shop during Open Enrollment? Not sure if you’re eligible to shop the Marketplace for an Obamacare plan? Good news: Most people are! If you are a U.S. citizen, national or legal resident of the United States who currently resides in the U.S., you’re qualified to shop the Marketplace. This includes green card holders, refugees, asylees, and individuals with non-immigrant status who have a valid worker visa. The only exceptions? If you’re currently enrolled in Medicare or currently incarcerated. Grab our free step-by-step guide to enrolling in Marketplace coverage to learn more. Keep in mind that if you are offered ACA-compliant health insurance by your employer and choose to opt-out of it and instead purchase your own Obamacare plan, you usually won’t be eligible for any subsidies and will need to pay full price for your monthly premiums. Because of this, if you have access to health insurance coverage through your employer, we recommend you utilize that instead of the Marketplace, unless your employer insurance costs more than 9.61% of your household income. For everyone else, though, welcome to shopping the Marketplace during OEP! We’ve tried to compile all the essential information you’ll need to make this year’s OEP as seamless as possible for you. Remember that should you have any questions at all, the HealthSherpa Consumer Advocate Team is here to help and can be reached at 872-228-2549. You can shop available plans and compare plan premiums here . Enrolling on HealthSherpa only takes an average of 15 minutes. During Open Enrollment Period, anyone who’s eligible can enroll in a Marketplace health plan. The rest of the year is known as Special Enrollment Period (SEP), and you’ll need a Qualifying Life Event (QLE) such as losing your health coverage, having a child, getting married, or another change in household size or health coverage. When can I shop the Marketplace during Open Enrollment? In most states, Open Enrollment Period runs from November 1st, 2020 to December 15, 2020. Some states, however, have extended their Open Enrollment Period. This means that anyone living in these states will have extra time to enroll. Regardless of which state you live in, you can shop for a 2021 plan at any point during Open Enrollment. So far for the 2021 OEP, the following states have extended Open Enrollment Periods to the following dates: Minnesota: Dec 22, 2020 Colorado: Jan 15, 2021 Nevada: Jan 15, 2021 Pennsylvania: Jan 15, 2021 Washington: Jan 15, 2021 Massachusetts: Jan 23, 2021 Rhode Island: Jan 23, 2021 California: Jan 31, 2021 District of Columbia: Jan 31, 2021 New Jersey: Jan 31, 2021 New York: Jan 31, 2021 We will update this list as any other states announce extended Open Enrollment Periods. Will I have to pay a fine if I don’t have health insurance in 2021? Congress repealed the penalty for having health insurance in 2018. That means in most states, you won’t have to pay a fine if you go without coverage in 2021. However, California, Massachusetts, New Jersey, Rhode Island, and DC have passed their own individual mandates. This means you may have to pay a penalty to the state if you go without coverage for a certain period of time. No matter which state you live in, it’s important to remember that health insurance limits your financial risk. All Marketplace plans have an annual out of pocket maximum, which means that if you receive high medical bills, you’ll only pay a portion of the cost. After I enroll during Open Enrollment Period, when does my health insurance begin? Almost everyone who enrolls during Open Enrollment Period (OEP) will have insurance coverage beginning on January 1, 2021. This coverage will continue until Dec. 31, 2021 as long as all monthly premium payments are made. If you gain other coverage during this period—for example, through a new job—you can cancel your Marketplace plan at any time. Did you enroll for Obamacare in a state with an extended OEP? Then your coverage may have a different start date. Check with your local state exchange for more details about your start date if you enroll during the extended enrollment period. What do I need when I’m ready to enroll? You’ll need some basic information on-hand to get started with the Open Enrollment process. First, you’ll need to provide information about your household, including household size (including anyone you claim on your tax return). For each of these people, you’ll need some basic information like birth dates, home addresses, and social security numbers. Additionally, you’ll need information about your best estimate for your 2021 income, information on how you file your taxes if you have a spouse, information about your sources of income, and policy numbers from any current health insurance plans. A note on immigration status Although you’re providing information about every member of your tax household, you do not have to provide immigration status unless you yourself are applying for coverage. If you don’t have a social security number, you also do not need to provide this on your Marketplace application. It’s important to know that information about immigration status collected by the Marketplace is carefully protected and cannot be used for immigration enforcement. More generally, by law the personal information that you provide on this form can only be used to determine your eligibility for coverage and to enroll you in a plan, and must be stored securely. If anyone in your household is a Permanent Resident, you’ll need their Resident Alien (A-number) ready. Typically, you will just need to enter the number, but you may need to upload the document so have it ready to scan in case you need it. You can find out about what documents you will need for other eligible immigration statuses here . What if I already have a plan from last year? If you had Marketplace health insurance in 2020, you will be automatically re-enrolled in that plan for next year if that plan is still being offered. If that plan is no longer available, you’ll be enrolled in an “equivalent” plan. Although that might sound like the easiest way to approach OEP, it isn’t necessarily your best option. In fact, people who who shop and switch plans save an average of 38% on their monthly premiums. Most insurers are expanding their coverage areas this year, which means there will be more plans available to you. Without shopping to compare what plans, and savings, are available to you this year, your premium payments may increase substantially. Plan details can change from year to year, too, meaning that prescription coverage, provider networks, and coverage benefits could change even if you keep the same plan. By shopping the Marketplace, you’ll find out what kinds of available plans might best suit your needs for the coming year, and what cost savings you will be eligible for with those plans. It only takes a few minutes to shop and compare your options, and this can keep you from paying more later. What about subsidies, cost-sharing reductions, and tax credits? Many Americans are eligible to save on their health insurance costs as a result of the Affordable Care Act. No matter where you live, if you earn between 100 – 400% of the Federal Poverty Level (determined by the federal government) and aren’t eligible for Medicaid , you will qualify for a premium tax credit that will help lower your premium costs. By 2020’s FPL numbers , this meant that a family of four whose combined household income was between $26,200 and $104,800 would qualify for a premium tax credit. Depending on your income, you may also qualify for Cost Sharing Reductions (CSR), which are special savings built-in to Silver-level Marketplace plans for people who earn between 100 and 250% of the federal poverty limit. These CSRs limit and reduce out-of-pocket costs like copays and deductibles. Remember that if you are married and do not file taxes jointly with your spouse, you will not be eligible for any subsidies or CSRs in the Marketplace. How do I sign-up for Marketplace insurance during Open Enrollment? Want to enroll in Marketplace insurance for 2021 but not sure where to start? We have a step-by-step breakdown of how to shop the Marketplace and what that process looks like here . In short, you can self-enroll online , have a Consumer Advocate help you over the phone, find local, in-person assistance , or complete and mail-in a paper application. Applying online through HealthSherpa, a certified enrollment partner of the government, is straightforward and simple. If you’re unfamiliar with HealthSherpa, know that we offer all of the same plans at the exact same prices as HealthCare.gov, the government’s enrollment site. The difference? We offer a simpler enrollment process, a website that’s easier to use, and have a phenomenal Consumer Advocate team on-hand to help you at each step along the way. Reachable by phone, email, and online chat, our Consumer Advocate Team are here to help both before and after you sign up for your new Obamacare plan. Our advocates are licensed health insurance experts with a background in advocacy, not salespeople. It only takes an average of around 15 minutes to complete an application on HealthSherpa, versus an average of 56 minutes when using Healthcare.gov . Of course if you have any questions before Open Enrollment begins or would like assistance in choosing a plan, please feel free to call our Consumer Advocate Team anytime at (872) 228-2549 . We’re here to help you navigate the Open Enrollment Period process and find the best possible plan for your needs. You can see plans and prices, and see how much financial help you’re eligible for, by entering your zip below. What about other coverage options like Medicare and Medicaid? You can apply for Medicaid year-round here—there’s no need to wait for an Open Enrollment Period. You can apply for Medicaid here . If you’d like to enroll in Medicare, you’ll become eligible three months before your 65th birthday, and you may become eligible earlier if you have certain disabilities. You can learn more about Medicare here . If you’re already enrolled in a Medicare plan and you’d like to make changes to it, Medicare open enrollment runs from October 15 to December 7. During this annual enrollment period (AEP), you can make changes to your coverage, such as switch between Original Medicare and a Medicare Advantage plan, or vice versa. If you have any questions, give our Consumer Advocate Team a call at (872) 228-2549 .
